clue.text: Reindeer quietly dashed to a playing field turning back

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
dashed means ran, hurried

indicators.note: turning back tells us to read the word for the playing field from right to left

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a British name for a public playing field

explanation.surface: Someone hurried quietly across to the sports field before turning round and heading back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses REC to CER. 'to' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the named reindeer that pull Santa's sleigh in the Christmas poem.

clue.text: Bear, damn it, a pompous official

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear
bah is an exclamation of annoyance, like damn it

explanation.surface: Someone swears at having to tolerate a self-important functionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like 'put up with'; it is Milne's teddy. The answer is the Lord High Everything Else in Gilbert and Sullivan's 'The Mikado'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's character holds every office at once, so his name means a self-important functionary.

clue.text: Ms Loos's collection of anecdotes about sex

definitions.note: the possessive reads as the name of Ms Loos with 's for is

indicators.note: about says the word for collection of anecdotes goes round the other piece

parts.note: ana is a collection of sayings or anecdotes about someone
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: The writer Loos has gathered stories about sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is': Ms Loos's first name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anita Loos wrote 'Gentlemen Prefer Blondes', so her first name stands for her.

clue.text: Journalist disrupting erotic do

indicators.note: disrupting says the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A reporter barges in and breaks up a racy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupting' looks like a journalist breaking into the party; it is the anagram signal for EROTIC DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper editor who shares the job with another is a kind of newspaper person.

clue.text: What Sadie Thompson experienced that's right fashionable about the East of Samoa

indicators.note: the East of says take the easternmost, that is final, letter of Samoa

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A trendy visitor to eastern Samoa found out what Maugham's heroine went through.
explanation.walkthrough: Sadie Thompson is the heroine of Somerset Maugham's story set on Samoa in the wet season; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maugham's story about Sadie Thompson is set during relentless downpours on Pago Pago.

clue.text: Act the part of a young man, Christy Mahon for example

parts.note: to act the part of is to play it
a boy is a young man

explanation.surface: An actor is cast as a youth and is told the role is Synge's hero Christy Mahon.
explanation.walkthrough: Christy Mahon is the hero of J. M. Synge's play 'The Playboy of the Western World'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synge's title calls his hero the pleasure-seeking young man of the western world, so he is an example of the type.

clue.text: What Fleming discovered, reformulated in nice pill

indicators.note: reformulated says the letters are put together in a different formula

explanation.surface: Fleming's discovery is remade in a handy tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleming' here is Alexander, not Ian; 'reformulated' rearranges IN NICE PILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Fleming found the first antibiotic in mould in 1928.

clue.text: One seen perhaps about end of scena in Purcell opera

definitions.note: the definition stands for a character in Purcell's opera Dido and the Trojan hero

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: about says the jumbled piece goes round the last letter of scena
perhaps hints the letters of seen may be arranged some other way
end of says take the final letter of scena

explanation.surface: A singer is spotted near the end of a scene in a Purcell opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns SEEN into ENES; 'about' puts it round A, the last letter of scena.
explanation.definitionFit: Purcell's opera Dido and Aeneas has the Trojan hero as Dido's lover, so he is one in it.

clue.text: Tuscan writer of verse in which a snake eats a small amount, then more of the same in front of a Greek nymph

indicators.note: in front of places the repeated piece ahead of the nymph in the row
eats says the snake swallows the small amount, which ends up inside

parts.note: a boa is a large snake
cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small amount of liquid
more of the same says repeat the small amount, cc again
Io is the nymph loved by Zeus in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A Tuscan poet's verse tells of a serpent swallowing a little before reaching a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' and 'then' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Boccaccio of Certaldo wrote the Decameron and much poetry, such as the Filostrato.

clue.text: One time leader Boris, degenerate in style

indicators.note: degenerate says the letters fall apart into a corrupted order

explanation.surface: A former leader called Boris has slid into decadence in his manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degenerate' looks like a description of Boris; it is the anagram signal for IN STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was the first president of the Russian Federation, from 1991 to 1999.

clue.text: Roland's friend, one accompanying an adherent of Cromwell

indicators.note: accompanying says the piece for one goes alongside the next piece in the row

parts.note: in the Song of Roland, Oliver is Roland's companion and friend
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medieval knight's comrade stands beside a Roundhead follower of the Lord Protector.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of Oliver Cromwell is named from his first name, as a Thatcherite is from a surname.

clue.text: Actor Williamson seen featuring in histrionic oldie

indicators.note: featuring in says the name appears inside the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A theatrical old film is spotted starring the actor Williamson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicol Williamson was a Scottish stage and screen actor, so his first name fits the definition.

clue.text: Adventure location for Fleming and another writer, Angela

definitions.meaning: Peter Fleming, Ian's brother, wrote a travel book about an adventure in the largest South American country
Angela, author of girls' boarding-school stories, has the country's name as her surname

explanation.surface: A list of literary places pairs Fleming's adventure setting with a writer called Angela.
explanation.definitionFit: The country names Peter Fleming's 1933 travel book and is also the surname of the school-story novelist Angela.

clue.text: Greeks, acording to Homer, beginning to approve what sounds like long periods of time at church

indicators.note: beginning to says take only the opening letter of approve
what sounds like says the word for long periods of time is spelt as it is heard

parts.note: aeons are immensely long periods of time

explanation.surface: A churchgoer approves of Homer's way of naming the Greeks over long ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word placing CH beside the sound-alike piece. The clue's 'acording' is the printed spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad calls the Greek army by the tribal name of the Achaeans rather than Hellenes.

clue.text: Badly flogged in finale of thriller, one by Fleming

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the next words are put together wrongly
finale of says take only the final letter of thriller

explanation.surface: A Fleming thriller ends with someone being cruelly flogged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's 1959 novel about a gold-obsessed villain is one of his Bond books.

clue.text: Musical greeting to Barbie, say

definitions.meaning: a Broadway show by Jerry Herman starring Carol Channing
Barbie is an example of a doll, so a hello said to her is this

explanation.surface: Someone says hi to a famous plastic toy in song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jerry Herman stage show's title is literally a salutation addressed to a toy figure such as Barbie.

clue.text: Bond subsequently becoming a writer

parts.note: a bond is a link or tie
subsequently means later

explanation.surface: James Bond later turns into an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like Fleming's spy but means a tie; 'becoming' is a link word. Eric Linklater was a Scottish novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Linklater was a Scottish novelist, author of 'Juan in America'.

clue.text: Image computer offers primarily to note a program symbolically

definitions.text: Image computer offers primarily to note a program symbolically

indicators.note: primarily says take the leading letter of each of the words around it

explanation.surface: A computer offers a small picture that stands for a program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'a program symbolically' carry no letters: the whole clue also describes the screen symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer screen a small pictorial symbol is clicked to open a program.

clue.text: Injured leg I held in Civil War battle

indicators.note: injured says the letters are damaged and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier wounded in the leg was captured at a Civil War battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The English Civil War is meant: its first pitched battle was fought in Warwickshire in 1642.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill, in October 1642, was the opening pitched battle of the English Civil War.

clue.text: Materials we hear for a Mozart symphony

indicators.note: we hear says the word for materials is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: lints are fabrics, especially linen, used for dressing wounds

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they hear fabrics named as a Mozart symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. Mozart's Symphony No. 36 is named after the Austrian city where he wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No. 36 is nicknamed after the Austrian city where it was composed and first played.

clue.text: Knocking up one who created Doctor Dolittle

definitions.meaning: hitting a ball high into the air, as in cricket or golf
Hugh, the author of the Doctor Dolittle books for children

explanation.surface: A children's author is busy knocking something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting a ball high is a cricket and golf term, and Hugh of that surname wrote the talking-animal doctor books.

clue.text: Dickensian press chief to turn cross

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective standing for a Dickens character and title

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
to wind is to turn a handle or key
a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in a church's rood screen

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss in a Dickens novel is about to become angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry'; it is a crucifix. The definition is Dickens's last, unfinished novel and its title character.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mystery of Edwin Drood is Dickens's unfinished final novel, so its hero is a figure of Dickens's making.

clue.text: Oxford mathematician, college fellow restraining wild dogs

indicators.note: restraining says the college fellow holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college

indicators.note: wild says the letters of dogs run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An Oxford mathematician from a college has to hold back some unruly dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oxford mathematician is Lewis Carroll under his real name; 'wild' is the anagram signal, and 'restraining' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lutwidge, better known as Lewis Carroll, taught mathematics at Christ Church, Oxford.

clue.text: "A prodigy of fear and a portent / Of broached mischief to the —— times" (Henry IV, Part 1)

definitions.text: "A prodigy of fear and a portent / Of broached mischief to the —— times" (Henry IV, Part 1)

parts.words: "A prodigy of fear and a portent / Of broached mischief to the —— times" (Henry IV, Part 1)
parts.note: a quotation clue: the missing word in Worcester's speech to the King, describing times yet to come

explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's line the missing word describes times still to come, not yet brought into being.

clue.text: Minor life mostly recreated in cinematic genre

indicators.note: recreated says the letters are made again in a new order
mostly says the word life loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A small life story is remade as a moody cinema piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LIFE to LIF; 'recreated' turns MINOR plus LIF into the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of dark crime movie of the 1940s and 1950s, named by French critics.

clue.text: Proteus, for instance, does a bit of great shape-shifting

indicators.note: shape-shifting says the letters change their form into a new arrangement
bit of says take just the first letter of great

explanation.surface: Proteus, famous for changing form, performs a small piece of great transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shape-shifting' is the anagram signal and also Proteus's famous gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteus is the shape-changing old man of the sea in Greek myth, a marine deity.

clue.text: Dress old woman who wanted to be left alone

definitions.text: woman who wanted to be left alone

parts.note: garb means clothing or dress

explanation.surface: An old woman's dress says she wished to be left in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman is Greta, the Swedish film star whose line 'I want to be alone' became her motto.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish film star Greta famously said she wanted solitude and retired early from Hollywood.

clue.text: Quietly and humbly, David Mamet tells us this needs speed

definitions.text: David Mamet tells us this needs speed

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
low means humble, lowly

explanation.surface: Quietly and modestly, a playwright tells us something has to go faster.
explanation.walkthrough: David Mamet's play is 'Speed-the-Plow', with the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Mamet's play title asks success for the farming implement, spelt the American way.

clue.text: Early part of a book one's torn up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: up here means disturbed or upset, signalling the letters of torn are jumbled

explanation.surface: The opening pages of a book have been ripped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TORN into NTRO; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for introduction, the opening section of a book.

clue.text: More than one old-fashioned dance involving two learners is a drag

indicators.note: involving, in its old sense of entangling, mixes the letters together

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate, so two learners are two Ls

explanation.surface: Someone finds all those old dances tedious, especially with two beginners joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' entangles LL with the letters of IS A DRAG into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively Renaissance court dances in triple time, in the plural.

clue.text: Tear up an inferior publication about an author of James Bond novels

indicators.note: about says the word for an inferior publication is turned round

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper

indicators.note: in a down entry up reverses; here it says the word for tear is read backwards

parts.note: to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: Someone rips up a trashy paper that wrote about a Bond novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAG to GAR and 'up' turns REND to DNER.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gardner wrote over a dozen continuation novels about Fleming's spy after Fleming's death.

clue.text: Fleming's neighbour starting to write everything on double-o seven at last

indicators.note: starting to says take the opening letter of write

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: double, joined to the letter by a hyphen, says the letter o is written twice

parts.note: taken as written, the letter O

indicators.note: at last says take only the final letter of seven

explanation.surface: Ian Fleming's neighbour begins to write all about agent 007.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleming' is not Ian but a Flemish speaker of Belgium; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Belgium the French-speaking people of the south live beside the Flemish-speaking people of Flanders.
